programs.title: Smart Parking, Safe Jobs: Agents and Worker Voice at 1111 Lincoln Road
programs.grade_or_level: Adult workforce / continuing education (building, parking and transport workers)
outcomes: Explain how an agent-managed, human-governed DAO routes tasks and drafts proposals while people hold final votes
Map parking and facilities job tasks to agent roles like Task Router and Progress Tracker
Draft a worker-authored proposal for the Proposal Forum
Identify governance actions reserved for humans only

sessions.activity: Tour the charter: mission, contribution model and reserved human actions; workers annotate which decisions affect their jobs.
Hands-on with the Task Router: workers simulate routing a maintenance task to a working group and log handoffs.
Compare evidence summaries from the Evidence Monitor against shop-floor knowledge; mark gaps and uncertainties.
Small groups draft a one-page proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter; humans debate, agents never enact.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized task-routing times and handoff counts from the simulation, plus de-identified worker feedback tags on agent-drafted summaries, contributed to shared models of human-agent task coordination.
programs.consent: Participation is voluntary and off the clock or with paid training time. Adults sign an informed consent form describing anonymization; union stewards review any data release; workers may withdraw and have their contributions deleted at any time.

programs.title: Civic Tech Detectives: Parking, Governance and the Open-Air Garage
outcomes: Describe the 1111 Lincoln Road garage as an urban landmark and explain why open-air design matters in Miami Beach's coastal climate
Explain the difference between what AI agents do and what only people may decide in a DAO
Collect and visualize simple parking or mobility observations
Present a mini-proposal to a mock Proposal Forum

sessions.activity: Read the charter mission; students sort decision cards into 'agents can do' vs 'only people vote' piles.
Students act as Evidence Monitors: gather facts about the garage from the brief and flag what is unknown vs. invented.
Build a simple progress tracker poster with measurable outcomes for a school-yard improvement idea.
Teams pitch mini-proposals; class holds the final vote, mirroring human-only governance.

programs.data_shared: De-identified class tallies from the decision-card sorting activity and anonymized proposal-topic counts, contributed as example datasets for shared civic-education models. No individual student data.
programs.consent: Signed guardian/parent consent is required for all data contributions; a school-approved media and privacy form covers photos and work samples. Teachers verify no personal identifiers are included; guardians may opt out at any time and student work is removed on request.

programs.title: Governance Without Gatekeepers: DAO Methods for Mission Teams
programs.grade_or_level: Professional / NGO staff and program leads
outcomes: Apply the agent-managed, human-governed model to an NGO decision workflow
Use zones (Charter Hall to Progress Observatory) as an organizational template
Define measurable outcomes and a contribution model for a program charter
Recognize the six human-reserved governance actions and design safeguards around them

sessions.activity: Workshop: draft a mini-charter with mission, measurable outcomes and explicitly reserved human decisions.
Role-play a decision cycle: agents draft, staff debate, leadership (humans) hold the final vote.
Map one real NGO workflow onto Task Router and Collaborator Scout roles; identify friction points.
Define 3-5 indicators and build a tracking template with the Progress Tracker pattern.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized workflow-mapping results and de-identified friction-point tags across participating teams, contributed to shared models of human-agent organizational design.
programs.consent: Organizations sign a data-sharing agreement specifying anonymization and aggregation before any contribution; individual staff participation is opt-in; teams can withdraw their workflow data at any time.

programs.title: From Landmark to Learning Lab: Nonprofit Programs at the Parking Smart.X Cell
programs.grade_or_level: Nonprofit program designers and volunteer coordinators
outcomes: Design a place-based program using the 1111 Lincoln Road garage and its five zones
Connect a nonprofit mission to measurable charter outcomes tracked in the Progress Observatory
Practice agent-assisted drafting with human-only enactment rules
Build a volunteer contribution model modeled on the DAO's structure

sessions.activity: Study the contribution model; each nonprofit drafts its own contributor ladder linking volunteers to outcomes.
Use the Evidence Monitor pattern to build a literature scan template for the nonprofit's cause area.
Draft a grant concept note with the Proposal & Grant Drafter role; peers critique; humans decide enactment.
Set up an outcomes dashboard template and agree on review cadence between decision cycles.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized program-design templates and de-identified outcome-indicator sets from participating nonprofits, contributed to shared open models of nonprofit program design. No beneficiary data.
programs.consent: Program leads sign a memorandum covering anonymized sharing; all contributed materials are scrubbed of beneficiary and donor identifiers; any nonprofit can request removal of its templates at any time.
